title: Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB)

summary: The Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB) rate stood at 3.65% as of April 21, 2026, unchanged from the prior observation date. The rate has remained flat at 3.65% for at least five consecutive business days (April 17–21). IORB is the interest rate the Federal Reserve pays to depository institutions on their reserve balances held at the Fed.
key_points: Rate has been flat at 3.65% for at least five consecutive trading days (April 17–21)
IORB functions as a floor in the federal funds market, effectively anchoring the top of the Fed's target range
why_it_matters: IORB is a key component of the Federal Reserve's monetary policy operating framework. As the rate paid on excess reserves, it influences banks' incentive to lend reserves in the overnight market. It effectively constrains the effective federal funds rate from exceeding the IORB, making it a structural anchor for short-term funding markets. Traders and risk managers monitor IORB to understand the Fed's policy rate ceiling.
market_structure_context: IORB represents the primary policy rate tool for the Fed's floor system. The flat reading suggests no change to the Fed's administered rate in recent days. This data point is a constituent of the Fed's overnight reverse repo (ON RRP) and federal funds market plumbing; IORB typically sits at the top of the federal funds target range.
